AUR helpers: Paru and Yay

The AUR provides user-submitted build scripts, which are not the same as prebuilt packages from the official repositories. AUR helpers are not officially supported and do not replace a review of PKGBUILD, installation scripts, and changes.

Review and clean builds
Why review a PKGBUILD?

A PKGBUILD is itself executable shell code: reading files, accessing the network, and running other programs can all happen during the build. Do not run makepkg as root or build unreviewed scripts in a working directory that contains sensitive credentials.
Clean chroots with devtools

The main purpose of a clean chroot is to provide consistent build dependencies and environments, preventing packages installed on the host from hiding missing dependencies. It is not equivalent to a sandbox with no network, no host mounts, or absolute protection from malicious code. Untrusted builds can be further confined to a dedicated virtual machine or a restricted account/environment.
Performance settings in makepkg.conf

Adjust parallel compilation to suit available memory. High compression levels increase packaging time and resource use, so use them only when smaller artifacts are genuinely needed. Experiment in the user-level makepkg configuration rather than treating machine-specific settings as optimal for every system.
Reproducible builds and distribution integrity
Reproducible builds concern whether the same inputs and environment produce identical artifacts. archlinux-repro is one of the relevant tools:

The repro verify <package_name> command from the original notes cannot be assumed to work across versions. Identical artifacts are evidence of reproducibility; they do not by themselves prove that source code is free of malicious behavior. Package signature verification, trusted keys, source code review, and independent rebuilds each serve different purposes.
The package management workflow
When synchronizing repository databases, perform a full system upgrade: sudo pacman -Syu. Do not use pacman -Sy package and create an unsupported partial upgrade.
